stem: A 7-year-old child has a full blood count showing a markedly raised lymphocyte count with anaemia and thrombocytopaenia; what is the most appropriate next step to clarify the white cell finding?

options.text: Assume this is reactive lymphocytosis and discharge
Repeat the analyser later without any further review
Order an ultrasound as the first investigation
Interpret the result as isolated monocytosis

explanation: Request a blood film review. This is because a markedly raised analyser-reported lymphocyte count with anaemia and thrombocytopaenia can represent leukaemic blasts, and a blood film is needed to clarify the white cell population.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a blood film can identify blasts or other abnormal cells that may be misclassified by the analyser as lymphocytes.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this pattern is not safely dismissed as reactive when anaemia and thrombocytopaenia are also present.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because repeating the analyser does not clarify whether the counted cells are true lymphocytes or blasts.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because ultrasound does not determine the nature of the abnormal white cell count.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because monocytosis is a different pattern and does not explain a markedly raised lymphocyte count with cytopenias.
